questions.question: Which children's novel by Anita Desai received the Guardian Children's Fiction Prize?

options.text: Where Shall We Go This Summer?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Village by the Sea**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Village by the Sea** is an acclaimed children's novel written by the distinguished Indian author **Anita Desai** and was first published in **1982**.
 
• The story is set in the small, traditional fishing village of **Thul**, located on the **Konkan coast** of **Maharashtra**, India.
 
• The plot centers on the struggles of two siblings, **Lila** and **Hari**, as they navigate the difficulties of **poverty**, their mother's illness, and their father's alcoholism in a rapidly industrializing society.
 
• The novel explores the tension between **rural traditions** and **urbanization**, specifically through **Hari’s** journey to **Bombay** (now Mumbai) to find work and save his family.
 
• Due to its profound emotional depth and realistic portrayal of Indian life, the book was awarded the **Guardian Children's Fiction Prize** in **1983**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Games at Twilight** (1978):

 
 
• This is a collection of **short stories** that focuses on the psychological nuances of childhood and the subtle complexities of family dynamics in **post-independence India**.
 
 
 
• **Diamond Dust and Other Stories** (2000):
 
 
• A later collection of fiction that examines themes of **isolation**, cultural displacement, and the mundane tragedies of everyday life across different continents.
 
 
 
• **Where Shall We Go This Summer?** (1975):
 
 
• A novel that tracks the internal crisis of **Sita**, a woman who seeks a spiritual or emotional retreat on an island to escape the stifling environment of her **urban existence**.
 
 
 
• **Anita Desai** is a multiple-time nominee for the **Booker Prize**, with her works **Clear Light of Day**, **In Custody**, and **Fasting, Feasting** reaching the shortlist.

questions.question: Which of the following is an autobiographical poem by William Wordsworth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Prelude**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Prelude** is widely recognized as the definitive **autobiographical poem** written by **William Wordsworth**, serving as an exploration of the **growth of a poet's mind**.
 
• The poem is written in **blank verse** and details Wordsworth's spiritual and intellectual development from his **childhood** and **Cambridge years** to his experiences during the **French Revolution**.
 
• Wordsworth began composing the work in **1798** and continued to revise it throughout his life, reflecting his evolving philosophy on **nature** and the **human imagination**.
 
• The poem was originally intended to be the introductory section of a larger, unfinished philosophical work entitled **The Recluse**.
 
• It was published posthumously in **1850**, and its title was suggested by the poet's widow, **Mary Wordsworth**, as the poet himself often referred to it as the 'poem to Coleridge'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Excursion**:

 
 
• Published in **1814**, this is a long philosophical poem in nine books intended to be the second part of **The Recluse** project.
 
 
 
• **The Recluse**:
 
 
• This was the planned tripartite **philosophical masterpiece** that Wordsworth never fully completed; it was meant to contain both **The Prelude** and **The Excursion**.
 
 
 
• **Michael**:
 
 
• A famous **pastoral narrative poem** published in the **1800** edition of **Lyrical Ballads**, which tells the story of an aging shepherd and his son **Luke**, set in the **Lake District**.

questions.question: In recent reports, which region usually scores the highest on the Happiness Index?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nordic countries (Northern Europe)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Happiness Report**, an annual publication by the **United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network**, consistently identifies **Northern Europe** as the happiest region globally.
 
• Nations such as **Finland**, **Denmark**, **Iceland**, **Norway**, and **Sweden** frequently occupy the top ten positions, with **Finland** often securing the first rank for multiple consecutive years.
 
• The high scores are attributed to six key variables: **GDP per capita**, **social support**, **healthy life expectancy**, **freedom to make life choices**, **generosity**, and **freedom from corruption**.
 
• These countries are characterized by high levels of **institutional trust** and **social cohesion**, where citizens feel a strong sense of security and communal belonging.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Nordic Model** of governance plays a pivotal role in these rankings:

 
 
• **Universal Welfare**: High-quality, state-funded **healthcare** and **education** reduce individual financial stress and promote **equity**.
 
• **Work-Life Balance**: Strong labor protections and generous **parental leave** policies contribute to higher life satisfaction.
 
• **Political Stability**: Stable **democratic institutions** and low levels of **political violence** ensure a predictable and safe environment for citizens.
 
• **Environmental Quality**: A strong emphasis on **sustainability** and access to **nature** is positively correlated with mental well-being in this region.
 
 
 
• Measurement Methodology:
 
 
• The index primarily uses the **Cantril Ladder**, where individuals rate their current life on a scale from 0 to 10.
 
• While **economic wealth** (GDP) is a factor, the report emphasizes that **social capital** and **personal autonomy** are often more significant drivers of happiness in advanced economies.

questions.question: In which year did the IAAF change its name to World Athletics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2019**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Association of Athletics Federations (IAAF)** officially rebranded itself as **World Athletics** in **2019**.
 
• The decision to change the name was approved during the **52nd IAAF Congress** held in **Doha**, Qatar, in **June 2019**.
 
• This rebranding initiative was led by the organization’s President, **Sebastian Coe**, as part of a broader strategy to make the sport more **modern**, **accessible**, and **marketable** to a global audience.
 
• The new brand identity, including a revamped **logo**, was fully implemented following the conclusion of the **World Athletics Championships** in **Doha** in **October 2019**.
 
• The name change also aimed to provide a clearer and more direct description of the organization’s role as the **global governing body** for the sport of athletics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Athletics**

 
 
• **Founding**: The organization was established on **July 17, 1912**, in **Stockholm, Sweden**, initially named the **International Amateur Athletic Federation**.
 
• **Evolution of Name**: In **2001**, the word 'Amateur' was replaced with 'Association' to reflect the professionalization of the sport, becoming the **International Association of Athletics Federations**.
 
• **Headquarters**: The central offices of the body have been located in **Monaco** since **1993**, after moving from London.
 
• **Core Functions**: It oversees the rules of the sport, manages the **World Athletics Series** of events, and maintains **world records** for track and field, road running, and race walking.
 
• **Leadership**: **Sebastian Coe**, a two-time Olympic champion, was elected as the **President** in **2015** and has focused on restoring the integrity of the sport through various **governance reforms**.

questions.question: Through which declaration was the subregional grouping that later evolved into BIMSTEC first established in 1997?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bangkok Declaration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subregional grouping that later evolved into **BIMSTEC** was established on **June 6, 1997**, through the signing of the **Bangkok Declaration** in **Thailand**.
 
• The organization was initially named **BIST-EC**, an acronym for the founding member states: **Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, and Thailand Economic Cooperation**.
 
• The **Bangkok Declaration** defined the group as a **bridge** between **South Asia** and **Southeast Asia**, emphasizing **technical and economic cooperation** among nations bordering the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• The primary objective was to create an enabling environment for rapid **economic development** and social progress through joint endeavors in sectors like **trade, investment, and technology**.
 
• The grouping expanded on **December 22, 1997**, when **Myanmar** became a full member, leading to the name change to **BIMST-EC**.
 
• With the admission of **Nepal** and **Bhutan** in **February 2004**, the organization was finally renamed the **Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Institutional Structure**

 
 
• The **BIMSTEC Secretariat** was established in **Dhaka, Bangladesh**, and was officially inaugurated in **2014**.
 
• The **Chairmanship** of BIMSTEC rotates among member states in **alphabetical order** of their names.
 
 
 
• **Member States and Geographical Scope**
 
 
• Currently, there are **seven member states**: five from South Asia (**Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, Sri Lanka**) and two from Southeast Asia (**Myanmar, Thailand**).
 
• This cooperation covers a diverse population of approximately **1.5 billion people** and a combined **GDP** of over **2.7 trillion USD**.
 
 
 
• **Context of Other Declarations**
 
 
• **Dhaka Declaration**: Primarily refers to the founding document of the **South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)** signed in **1985**.
 
• **Kathmandu Declaration**: Associated with the **18th SAARC Summit** in **2014**, focusing on **Regional Integration** for Peace and Prosperity.
 
• **Colombo Declaration**: Relates to various international agreements, most notably the **2019 declaration** for sustainable **Nitrogen management**.

questions.question: The famous “Hindu rate of growth” phrase was coined by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raj Krishna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Professor **Raj Krishna**, a prominent **Indian economist** and former member of the **Planning Commission**, coined the term **'Hindu rate of growth'** in **1978** at a seminar of the **Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI)**.
 
• The phrase was used to describe the **stagnant annual growth rate** of the **Indian economy**, which averaged around **3.5%** for several decades between the **1950s** and the **1980s**.
 
• During this period, despite various **Five-Year Plans**, the **per capita income** growth remained very low, averaging only about **1.3%** per annum due to high **population growth**.
 
• The term metaphorically suggested that the **slow pace of development** was a result of a **fatalistic** or **contented** cultural outlook, though it was actually a critique of the **restrictive economic policies** and the **License Raj**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Montek Singh Ahluwalia**:

 
 
• A key architect of the **1991 Economic Reforms** in India.
 
• He served as the **Deputy Chairman** of the **Planning Commission** and was the first **Director** of the **Independent Evaluation Office** at the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)**.
 
 
 
• **Jagdish Bhagwati**:
 
 
• An eminent **Professor of Economics** at **Columbia University** known for his advocacy of **free trade**.
 
• His work heavily influenced the transition of the Indian economy from **protectionism** to **globalization**.
 
 
 
• **Amartya Sen**:
 
 
• An **Indian economist** and **philosopher** who was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences** in **1998**.
 
• He is celebrated for his contributions to **welfare economics**, **social choice theory**, and his work on the causes of **famine** and **human development**.
 
 
 
• **License Raj**:
 
 
• Refers to the system of **elaborate licenses**, regulations, and **red tape** required to set up and run businesses in India between **1947** and **1990**.
 
• This system is widely cited as the primary reason for the **economic stagnation** associated with the **Hindu rate of growth**.

questions.question: Which index is used to measure headline inflation in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Consumer Price Index Combined**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Headline inflation** represents the total inflation in an economy, encompassing a wide basket of goods and services including volatile components like **food** and **fuel** prices.
 
• In **India**, the **Consumer Price Index (CPI) Combined** is currently utilized as the definitive measure for headline inflation. This shift was officially adopted by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** in **April 2014**.
 
• The adoption of **CPI Combined** (which includes both **rural** and **urban** data) followed the recommendations of the **Urjit Patel Committee**, which suggested moving away from the **Wholesale Price Index (WPI)** to better reflect the cost of living for citizens.
 
• The data for **CPI Combined** is released monthly by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**, which operates under the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**.
 
• The index uses a base year of **2012** and is the primary anchor for the **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** to maintain price stability with a target inflation rate of **4%** and a tolerance band of **plus/minus 2%**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wholesale Price Index (WPI)**:

 
 
• It tracks the changes in the price of goods sold and traded in bulk by wholesale businesses.
 
• The index is published by the **Office of Economic Adviser**, **Ministry of Commerce and Industry**.
 
• Unlike **CPI**, it does not account for the prices of **services**, focusing solely on physical commodities.
 
 
 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP) Deflator**:
 
 
• This is a comprehensive measure of inflation calculated as the ratio of **Nominal GDP** to **Real GDP** multiplied by 100.
 
• It covers all goods and services produced within the domestic economy, but it is typically available only on a **quarterly** or **annual** basis, unlike the monthly CPI.
 
 
 
• **Index of Industrial Production (IIP)**:
 
 
• It measures the growth in the volume of industrial production across sectors such as **Mining**, **Manufacturing**, and **Electricity**.
 
• It is an indicator of industrial activity and economic health rather than a direct measure of price inflation.

questions.question: Which traveller's account provides vivid descriptions of Muhammad bin Tughlaq and his reign?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ibn Battuta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ibn Battuta** was a renowned **Moroccan** explorer and scholar who traveled to India during the **14th century**.
 
• He arrived at the court of **Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq** in **1333 AD** after crossing the **Hindu Kush** mountains and reaching the **Indus River**.
 
• The Sultan, impressed by his expertise in **Islamic Law**, appointed him as the **Qazi** (Judge) of **Delhi**, a post he held for approximately eight years.
 
• His famous travelogue, written in **Arabic** and titled **Rihla** (The Journey), provides a comprehensive and vivid account of the **Tughlaq dynasty**, administrative practices, and the Sultan's complex personality.
 
• The **Rihla** documents significant historical events, including the **transfer of the capital** from **Delhi to Daulatabad** and the introduction of **token currency** using copper coins.
 
• His writings also offer deep insights into the **postal system** (Uluq and Dawa), the **caste system**, and the socio-economic conditions of **Medieval India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Al-Biruni**:

 
 
• An **Uzbek** polymath who accompanied **Mahmud of Ghazni** to the Indian subcontinent in the **11th century**.
 
• He authored the monumental work **Kitab-ul-Hind**, which serves as an encyclopedic source on Indian **astronomy**, **philosophy**, and **customs**.
 
 
 
• **Marco Polo**:
 
 
• A **Venetian** merchant and explorer who visited **South India** (the **Pandyan Kingdom**) around **1292 AD**.
 
• His accounts focus on the maritime trade, **pearl fisheries**, and the wealth of the **Coromandel Coast**.
 
 
 
• **Domingo Paes**:
 
 
• A **Portuguese** traveler who visited the **Vijayanagara Empire** around **1520 AD**.
 
• He provided detailed descriptions of the military strength and urban layout of **Hampi** during the reign of **Krishnadevaraya**.

questions.question: Since the Jal Jeevan Mission launch in 2019, more than _______ crore rural households have been provided tap water connection till July 2024.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM)** was launched by the **Government of India** on **August 15, 2019**, with the primary objective of providing safe and adequate drinking water through **Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTC)** to every rural household by **2024**.
 
• At the time of the mission's announcement, only about **3.23 crore** (roughly 16.7 percent) of the total **19.27 crore** rural households in the country had access to tap water connections.
 
• By **July 2024**, the mission crossed a major landmark by ensuring that more than **15 crore** rural households have access to clean tap water, representing a coverage of over **77 percent** of the rural population.
 
• The mission is designed as a **decentralized**, demand-driven, and community-managed program, emphasizing the **bottom-up approach** where the **Gram Panchayat** plays a pivotal role in planning and implementation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Operational Framework**:

 
 
• The mission is implemented by the **Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation** under the **Ministry of Jal Shakti**.
 
• It aims to provide **55 liters of water per capita per day (lpcd)** of prescribed quality (**BIS:10500** standards) on a long-term basis.
 
• The project includes **source sustainability** measures such as **recharge and reuse** through **greywater management**, water conservation, and **rainwater harvesting**.
 
 
 
• **Har Ghar Jal States**:
 
 
• Several states and Union Territories, including **Goa**, **Gujarat**, **Haryana**, **Punjab**, **Telangana**, **Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu**, and **Puducherry**, have achieved **100 percent** coverage.
 
• A village is officially declared **Har Ghar Jal Certified** once every household, school, and **Anganwadi center** is confirmed to have a functional tap connection by the **Gram Sabha**.

questions.question:
Which of the following is a component of DAJGUA Abhiyan?

I. Healthcare

II. Education
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **DAJGUA Abhiyan** is a targeted developmental initiative designed to uplift marginalized sections and enhance the quality of life in rural and tribal regions. Under its **Healthcare** component, the program aims to provide access to essential medical services, conduct immunisation campaigns, reduce infant and maternal mortality, and raise awareness about nutrition, personal hygiene, and clean drinking water. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• Under the **Education** component, the campaign focuses on improving literacy levels, facilitating the enrolment of children in schools, reducing school dropout rates especially among girls, and strengthening local educational infrastructure in far-flung areas. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **DAJGUA Abhiyan** employs a holistic, community-driven approach to guarantee the long-term sustainability of its developmental outcomes.

 
 
• **Socio-Economic Empowerment**: The campaign works to link rural households with various social welfare schemes, self-help groups (**SHGs**), and livelihood programmes.
 
• **Grassroots Governance**: It encourages local community participation and capacity building, training local youth and women to spearhead healthcare and education projects at the village level.

questions.question: An election to fill a vacancy in the office of President of India occurring by reason of his death, resignation or removal, or otherwise shall be held as soon as possible after, and in no case later than _____ months from, the date of occurrence of the vacancy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **Article 62(2)** of the **Constitution of India**, any vacancy caused by the **death**, **resignation**, or **removal** of the **President** must be filled through an election conducted as soon as possible.
 
• The Constitution mandates a definitive upper limit, stating that such an election must take place no later than **six months** from the date the vacancy occurs.
 
• This provision ensures that the post of the **Head of State**, which is the highest constitutional office in the country, does not remain vacant or be filled by an acting official for an extended duration.
 
• The newly elected **President** does not merely serve the remainder of the predecessor's term but is entitled to hold office for a full term of **five years** as per **Article 56**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Framework for Vacancies**:

 
 
• **Article 65**: Specifies that the **Vice-President** shall act as **President** until a new President is elected and enters upon their office.
 
• **Discharge of Functions**: If the **Vice-President**'s office is also vacant, the **Chief Justice of India** (or the senior-most judge of the **Supreme Court**) performs these duties under the **President (Discharge of Functions) Act, 1969**.
 
• **Article 62(1)**: Clarifies that an election to fill a vacancy caused by the normal expiration of the term must be completed **before the term expires**.
 
 
 
• **Election Administration**:
 
 
• The **Election Commission of India** (ECI) is the authority responsible for conducting the **Presidential Election**.
 
• The election is held in accordance with the **Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952** and the **Rules of 1974**.
 
• The process involves an **Electoral College** consisting of elected members of both Houses of **Parliament** and the **Legislative Assemblies** of the States.

questions.question: The first successful Indian Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle was _____ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PSLV-D2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV)** is a third-generation launch vehicle designed by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** to carry **Indian Remote Sensing (IRS)** satellites into **Sun-synchronous orbits**.
 
• The first developmental flight, **PSLV-D1**, was launched on **September 20, 1993**, from **Sriharikota**; however, the mission failed to place the **IRS-1E** satellite in orbit due to a guidance control error.
 
• The mission **PSLV-D2**, conducted on **October 15, 1994**, became the **first successful mission** in the PSLV series by successfully injecting the **IRS-P2** satellite into the desired polar orbit.
 
• The **IRS-P2** satellite weighed approximately **804 kg** and was placed into an orbit at an altitude of **817 km**, proving India's indigenous capability for complex space launches.
 
• This success marked India's transition into the elite group of nations capable of launching satellites into **Polar Sun-Synchronous Orbits**, which are critical for earth observation and resource mapping.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Technical Specifications of PSLV:**

 
 
• It is a **four-stage vehicle** that uses a combination of **solid and liquid propellants**. The first and third stages are solid, while the second and fourth stages are liquid.
 
• The second stage utilizes the famous **Vikas engine**, a high-thrust engine developed by **Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC)**.
 
• The vehicle has three main variants: **PSLV-G** (Generic), **PSLV-CA** (Core Alone), and **PSLV-XL**.
 
 
 
• **Other PSLV Missions:**
 
 
• **PSLV-C5**: Launched in **October 2003**, this operational flight successfully placed **IRS-P6 (Resourcesat-1)** into orbit, which was then the most advanced remote sensing satellite.
 
• **PSLV-C7**: Launched in **January 2007**, it was a landmark mission that carried **Cartosat-2** and the **Space Capsule Recovery Experiment (SRE-1)**, demonstrating India's **re-entry technology**.
 
• **PSLV-C15**: Launched in **July 2010**, it carried **Cartosat-2B** along with several international nano-satellites, showcasing the vehicle's versatility in carrying multiple payloads.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• Known as the **'Workhorse of ISRO'**, the PSLV has launched iconic missions like **Chandrayaan-1** (2008) and the **Mars Orbiter Mission** (2013).
 
• It holds a world record for launching **104 satellites** in a single mission (**PSLV-C37**) in **2017**.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is NOT correct?

options.text: The states of matter are inter-convertible.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Evaporation causes heating**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Statement 1 suggests that evaporation results in an increase in temperature; however, in thermodynamics, **evaporation** is essentially a **cooling process**. During this phase change, liquid molecules absorb energy, known as the **latent heat of vaporization**, from their surroundings or the surface they contact, leading to a temperature reduction in that area. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement 2 describes the **inter-convertibility** of matter. Substances can transition between **solid, liquid, and gas** states through variations in **temperature** and **pressure**, facilitating processes such as **melting**, **freezing**, and **sublimation**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Statement 3 classifies **boiling** as a **bulk phenomenon**. When a liquid reaches its **boiling point**, the energy is distributed throughout the entire volume, allowing molecules within the interior to form vapor bubbles and escape. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Statement 4 identifies **evaporation** as a **surface phenomenon**. Unlike boiling, this process occurs only at the interface between the liquid and the air, where molecules with higher **kinetic energy** overcome **intermolecular forces** to escape into the atmosphere. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Factors Affecting Evaporation**:

 
 
• **Surface Area**: The rate increases with a larger area as more molecules are exposed to the surface.
 
• **Humidity**: A decrease in humidity in the surrounding air increases the rate of evaporation.
 
• **Wind Speed**: Higher wind speeds move vapor particles away quickly, preventing saturation at the surface.
 
 
 
• **Phase Transitions**:
 
 
• **Sublimation**: The direct transition from solid to gas, bypassing the liquid state (e.g., **Camphor** or **Dry Ice**).
 
• **Latent Heat**: The hidden energy required to change the state of a substance without changing its temperature.
 
• **Vapor Pressure**: The pressure exerted by vapor when it is in equilibrium with its liquid phase at a specific temperature.

questions.question: Mediterranean agriculture is highly specialised ____ agriculture.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**commercial**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mediterranean agriculture** is a highly specialized and **capital-intensive** form of **commercial agriculture** practiced in regions surrounding the **Mediterranean Sea**, **California**, central **Chile**, the southwestern part of **South Africa**, and southwestern **Australia**.
 
• The system is uniquely designed to produce high-value crops for the **international market**, making it one of the most profit-oriented agricultural practices globally.
 
• **Viticulture**, or the cultivation of grapes, is the most distinctive specialty of this region; high-quality grapes are used for **wine production**, while others are dried into **raisins** and **currants**.
 
• The region serves as the **orchard of the world**, focusing on the large-scale production of **citrus fruits** (like oranges and lemons), **olives**, and **figs**, which are exported to colder northern climates.
 
• Geographical advantages such as **mild, wet winters** and **hot, dry summers** allow these regions to supply fresh fruits and vegetables to **European** and **North American** markets during the winter season when local production in those areas is impossible.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subsistence Agriculture**:

 
 
• Primary objective is meeting the consumption needs of the farmer and their family.
 
• Typically involves low levels of technology and minimal surplus for **trade** or **market exchange**.
 
 
 
• **Shifting Cultivation**:
 
 
• A primitive practice where land is cleared by **slashing and burning** vegetation.
 
• Farming continues until soil fertility declines, after which the farmer moves to a new plot, known as **Jhumming** in North-East India.
 
 
 
• **Pastoral Farming**:
 
 
• Focuses on the rearing of **livestock** (sheep, goats, cattle) rather than crop production.
 
• Often involves **transhumance**, where herders move animals between seasonal pastures.
 
 
 
• **Mediterranean Climate**:
 
 
• Known for the **Cs climate** type in the Koeppen classification, featuring **winter precipitation** and **xerophytic** vegetation like the **cork oak**.

questions.question: It was presumed that in the year _____, the game of basketball in India was started at the YMCA Calcutta.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1905**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The introduction of **basketball** to **India** is historically traced back to the early 20th century, closely following the sport's global expansion led by the **Young Men's Christian Association (YMCA)**.
 
• In **1905**, the game was officially presumed to have started at the **YMCA Calcutta** (now Kolkata), which served as a major center for the promotion of modern physical education in the country.
 
• The sport reached Indian shores through physical directors trained at the **Springfield College** in the United States, who were dispatched to various **YMCA** branches across the **British Raj**.
 
• **Calcutta**, being the capital of British India until 1911, was the primary gateway for many Western sports, including football and basketball, allowing them to gain early popularity among students and military personnel.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Invention and Global Context**:

 
 
• **Dr. James Naismith** invented basketball in **December 1891** at the International YMCA Training School in **Springfield, Massachusetts**.
 
• The game was initially played with **peach baskets** and a **soccer ball**, eventually evolving into the modern sport known today.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Basketball in India**:
 
 
• The **Basketball Federation of India (BFI)**, the governing body for the sport in the nation, was formally established in **1950**.
 
• The first **National Basketball Championship** was conducted in **1934** in **New Delhi**, organized under the aegis of the **Indian Olympic Association (IOA)**.
 
• The **Indian National Basketball Team** achieved its most significant historical milestone by qualifying for and participating in the **1980 Moscow Olympics**.
 
• India is a founding member of **FIBA Asia**, which was established in **1958** to manage basketball operations across the continent.
